items.title: Microsoft Pulled the Update That Switched Off Word and Excel
items.summary: Microsoft pulled a faulty update that switched off Word and Excel on home computers — people opened a document and were told their software was unlicensed, or found it gone. One repair shop had five customers hit within ten minutes, and I've had calls here too. Don't pay to fix it, and be wary of any message offering to do it for you — that's where the scam starts. Open Word or Excel, click Reactivate, and sign in with the account you normally use; if it's gone, reinstall the copy you bought.

items.title: Stop renting Microsoft Office — LibreOffice is the free office suite at libreoffice.org that opens Word, Excel and PowerPoint files and never sends your documents to AI
items.summary: Download LibreOffice free from libreoffice.org, install it, and it opens your Word, Excel and PowerPoint files just like the paid versions. There is no subscription, no account, and no AI reading your documents — it works completely on your own computer, even offline.

items.title: Can't hear the TV or a video on your computer? Windows 11's free Live Captions types out the words — turn it on with Windows key + Ctrl + L
items.summary: On a Windows 11 computer, press the Windows key, Ctrl, and L at the same time to turn on Live Captions, or open Settings > Accessibility > Captions and flip the Live captions switch. It is free and built in, and it shows on-screen text for any sound your computer plays — a video, a call, or a DVD.

items.title: Fake Bill-Pay Ads Are Stealing People's Payments
items.summary: Scammers are buying the ads at the top of search results when you look up a bill — power, water, or internet. You click a fake payment page that looks just like your provider's, pay it, and the money goes straight to a crook while your real bill sits unpaid. I check the address bar and type my provider's exact website myself instead of trusting the first ad. Pay only through the bill you were mailed, and report fakes at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

items.title: Windows 11 Search can finally drop Bing — flip off "web results" free in Settings > Privacy & security > Search
items.summary: Click Start, open Settings, click Privacy & security, then click Search. Turn off the switch called web results (and, if you like, the one called search highlights). That keeps the little search box focused on your own programs and files instead of fetching ads and web pages every time you type. It is free, it is already built into Windows, and it takes about a minute.

items.title: Windows has free built-in troubleshooters that solve sound, printer, and Wi-Fi problems for you — open Settings > System > Troubleshoot and click Run
items.summary: Click Start, open Settings, click System, then click Troubleshoot. Under Other troubleshooters, find the problem you are having — no sound, printer not working, Wi-Fi dropping — and click Run next to it. Windows will find the common cause and fix it for you. It is free, it is already on your computer, and nothing to buy or download.

items.title: A Fake 'Free Upgrade' Login Window Wants Your Password
items.summary: Scammers are offering a free upgrade to a paid AI tool, then showing a fake Google sign-in window to "claim" it. That window is drawn inside the website — it isn't really Google — so anything you type goes straight to the crooks. A real Google sign-in opens in your browser's own window, never floating inside a page. If one pops up inside a website, close the tab and never type your password. I type google.com myself whenever I'm unsure.

items.title: Your robot vacuum has a camera — the government just flagged a security flaw in Eufy robot vacuums, so update yours free in the eufy Clean app
items.summary: Open the free eufy Clean app — the same app you use to start and schedule your vacuum. Tap your vacuum on the screen, tap the three dots in the top right corner, and choose Firmware Update. Before you do, put the vacuum back on its charging base and make sure your home Wi-Fi is steady. It takes a few minutes, it is free, and you do not need to buy anything.

items.title: Firefox now gets a fresh, safer version every two weeks instead of once a month — keep yours current free in Menu, Help, About Firefox
items.summary: Open Firefox, click the Menu button in the top right corner — it is the three little lines — then click Help, then click About Firefox. A small window opens and Firefox checks for the newest version by itself. If one is waiting it downloads on its own, and you click Restart to update. That is the whole thing: free, no account, about a minute.

items.title: 600,000 Card Numbers Stolen From Online Checkouts
items.summary: Thieves have been slipping a few lines of sneaky code onto the checkout pages of more than a hundred online shops, so every card number typed in gets quietly copied to them. Over 600,000 cards have been taken since July, according to security researchers. The shops look normal — you can't spot this scam by looking. Check your last card statement today and report anything you don't recognize. I've switched to a credit card for online shopping, never a debit card — it's far easier to get your money back.

items.title: Is your computer running slow? Microsoft's free PC Manager tidies it up in one click — get it from the Microsoft Store or pcmanager.microsoft.com
items.summary: Go to pcmanager.microsoft.com — or open the Microsoft Store, search Microsoft PC Manager, and install it. It is free, and it is made by Microsoft rather than by some outfit selling you a yearly plan. Open it and press the big Boost button. It sweeps out temporary junk files, shows you which apps open by themselves the moment you turn the computer on, and runs a quick health check in one tap. Works on Windows 10 and Windows 11.

items.title: Google just plugged 108 security holes in Chrome — update yours free in one minute at chrome://settings/help
items.summary: Open Chrome, type chrome://settings/help into the address bar, and press Enter. Chrome looks for the newest version on its own, so you are not hunting for a download. If it says Chrome is up to date, you are done. If a newer version is waiting, it installs and shows you a Relaunch button — click it once and your browser reopens, already protected. Free, about a minute, and no account needed.
